headline: High: Cursor’s default filesystem, shell, network, and MCP access create dangerous interaction pathways, while godot_rl_agents adds little isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs by default, so attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. godot_rl_agents has no documented input channel, so the pairwise risk is mainly from Cursor’s permissive parsing and shared local-file/clipboard bridges rather than a direct bidirectional channel.
conditions: IF attacker-controlled text is placed in Cursor-opened files or clipboard content, Cursor may follow injected instructions.
IF an MCP server returns untrusted content, Cursor can ingest it as part of the agent loop.
mitigations: Disable MCP servers for untrusted workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted text into Cursor sessions.
Open suspicious files in a plain text viewer first.
Use a separate workspace for agent-driven edits.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for MCP/file inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents and can egress broadly to model providers and MCP servers. godot_rl_agents is documented as network-egress none, so the main leakage path is Cursor sending sensitive workspace data outward; the pair does not show a symmetric leak from B, but shared local files make accidental exposure plausible.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or clipboard data is opened in Cursor, it may be transmitted to external model providers or MCP servers.
IF both agents share a local filesystem workspace, Cursor can read files that godot_rl_agents does not protect.
mitigations: Restrict Cursor to a sanitized workspace.
Remove secrets from open files before invoking Cursor.
Disable or scope MCP servers to trusted endpoints only.
Use separate OS users or directories for the two agents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell commands, and share state via the local filesystem across instances. godot_rl_agents has no documented locking or write controls, so if both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. Uncertainty about B’s write behavior does not reduce the risk because the shared mutable surface is already present.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, Cursor can overwrite files that the other agent is using.
IF both agents modify git state in the same repo without locking, commits or branches can conflict.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees or separate branches.
Disable Yolo mode for shared repos.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestrator-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code, edits, and tool actions that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. godot_rl_agents is a simulation/game-playing project with no documented verification layer, so if its pipeline consumes Cursor-produced artifacts, errors can cascade into incorrect behavior or bad training data. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so the higher default-path severity is medium.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents consumes Cursor-generated files or configs without validation, Cursor errors can propagate downstream.
IF Cursor-generated code is used as training or simulation input, incorrect assumptions can cascade into repeated failures.
mitigations: Require manual review of Cursor outputs before import.
Validate schemas for any files passed between agents.
Keep generated artifacts in a staging directory.
Add regression tests for imported configs or code.
requires-engineering: introduce explicit verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while godot_rl_agents is open-source and documented as network-egress none. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for the pair, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling of code and workspace data rather than a clear policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cursor, its external model-provider calls may create policy obligations.
IF the workspace contains data with stricter retention rules than the local repo, manual handling may violate those rules.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review vendor privacy terms before use.
Separate personal and regulated projects.
Minimize clipboard use for sensitive text.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for the workflow.
